summary_for_children: An-Nasr says when Allah's help comes and people enter Islam in crowds, praise Allah and ask forgiveness.
environment_concept: Many paths from every direction meet at an open gate, marked with lanterns that come on one by one. Beyond it is a quiet terrace for praise. No people are shown: the paths stand for the multitudes.
architecture_and_scenery: Converging stone paths with lanterns, an open gateway, a terrace with a low wall.

areas.name: The Open Gate
areas.description: An open gateway at the end of the road, for reading 110:1.

areas.name: Converging Roads
areas.description: Many roads meeting from every direction, lit by lanterns. No people are shown.

areas.name: Terrace of Praise
areas.description: A quiet terrace to stop at and read 110:3.

activities.name: Thank and ask forgiveness

primary_mechanic.text: After finishing a big task, stop to praise and ask forgiveness before celebrating (110:3).

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: Gratitude After Success
story_library.children_narration: When Allah's help and victory come and people enter the religion in groups, the surah calls for praising Allah and seeking forgiveness. It reminds us that success should make us grateful, not arrogant.

world_idea.title: The Courtyard of Gratitude
world_idea.description: Explore a historically informed city setting and complete a reflection activity about humility after success. Do not depict Prophet Muhammad.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The Prophet and the people entering Islam are not shown.
